To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hybrid stochastic Galerking method is most efficient in terms of accuracy and number of model runs for the considered scenario.
the spatially adaptive sparse grid method is the most efficient approach for the considered problem and that all other methods tested are less efficient.

the kernel-based greedy interpolation and the hybrid stochastic Galerking method are the most accurate approaches for the given problem, but that the arbitrary polynomial chaos method is the most accurate method for a given number of model runs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to quantify uncertainty of model output for a given model and given data.
the question of how to best use the available data to obtain reliable estimates for the uncertainties in a model of a carbon dioxide storage site.
a comparison of four methods for uncertainty quantification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no method is superior to the others, but the choice of the method depends on the specific problem at hand.
no single method is superior to the others in all aspects.
there is no best method, but each method has advantages and drawbacks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the context of carbon dioxide storage, all methods considered in this work can be recommended to the modeler.
the hybrid stochastic Galerikin method is the most accurate approach for the benchmark scenario.
, in our case, the kernel-based method is the most efficient method in terms of accuracy versus number of samples, whereas the sparse grid method is the fastest one.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the choice of the uncertainty quantification method should be guided by the available information on the distribution shapes of uncertain parameters and the computational budget for a particular application.
all methods can yield accurate results for the benchmark scenario, but the computational cost differs significantly.
the choice of an uncertainty quantification method should be based on the available computational resources and the type of data that is used to construct the surrogate model.
